title: Jr. NTR's Dragon Glimpse Just Crossed 105 Million YouTube Views. Only Two Indian Films Have Done That Before.
excerpt: Prashanth Neel's 1960s assassin thriller set a first-day record of 64 million views and is now chasing Toxic for second place all-time.
body:
When Jr. NTR's birthday glimpse for *Dragon* dropped on May 20, it didn't just trend. It detonated. The four-minute first look clocked 64 million YouTube views in its opening 24 hours — the highest first-day debut for any Indian film glimpse ever recorded. Ten days later, it has crossed 105 million views across all language versions and officially entered the top three most-viewed movie glimpses in Indian cinema history.

Only two films sit above it: *Peddi*, the Allu Arjun and Nani starrer that holds the crown at 175 million-plus views, and *Toxic*, Yash's action vehicle at 110 million. At the rate *Dragon* is accumulating views, it's expected to surpass *Toxic* within days and claim the second spot.

## The Numbers Tell a Bigger Story

What makes *Dragon*'s reception especially significant for diaspora audiences is its reach beyond the Telugu-speaking belt. The Hindi-dubbed version alone has racked up over 25 million views and nearly 300,000 likes — numbers that signal genuine pan-India anticipation rather than regional fandom inflated by bots. For a Telugu film that hasn't even released a full trailer yet, that level of Hindi-market engagement is remarkable.

The glimpse introduces Jr. NTR as Luger, an assassin operating in the border regions between India, Bhutan, and China during 1967. Director Prashanth Neel — the man behind *KGF* and *Salaar* — has called this the "darkest story" he's ever written, and three years went into developing the character and its world before cameras started rolling.

## A Period Thriller in the Golden Triangle

Set against the backdrop of the international opium trade in the Golden Triangle, *Dragon* is a period action-thriller that looks nothing like the mass entertainers that typically dominate Telugu cinema. The gritty visuals, heavy industrial background score by Ravi Basrur, and Neel's signature larger-than-life presentation have drawn comparisons to his *KGF* universe — but with a darker, more global sensibility.

Jr. NTR's transformation is striking. The actor, last seen in *War 2*, sports a rugged, almost unrecognizable look as Luger. The character's name itself — a reference to the iconic German pistol — signals the film's international ambitions.

## Release and What's Next

*Dragon* is set to release worldwide on June 11, 2027, pushed back from its original June 2026 window due to the massive scale of production. The film is backed by Mythri Movie Makers and NTR Arts, with a significant portion of the shoot still pending. Casting for key roles is reportedly ongoing, and the delay suggests the makers are prioritizing craft over schedule.

For NRIs who grew up watching Jr. NTR evolve from a Telugu superstar into a global name after *RRR*, *Dragon* represents the next chapter. The YouTube numbers are an early indicator that when this film finally arrives in theaters, it won't just be a Telugu event — it'll be a pan-Indian one.

The all-time glimpse leaderboard now reads: *Peddi* at 175 million, *Toxic* at 110 million, and *Dragon* at 105 million and climbing. If *KGF Chapter 2* taught us anything about Prashanth Neel's ability to convert online hype into box office gold, the competition should be paying attention.
author: Diaspora Desk
